title: Number Systems for Placement

steps.title: Natural, whole, integers, rationals
steps.content: Natural numbers start at 1. Whole numbers include 0. Integers include negatives. Rational numbers can be written as p/q with q ≠ 0. Service-company papers mix classification with divisibility and remainders.
steps.tip: 0 is whole but not natural in the standard Indian exam convention.

steps.title: Classify the number
steps.explanation: −3 is an integer. It is not natural or whole.
hints: Natural numbers are positive counting numbers.

steps.title: Divisibility shortcuts
steps.content: A number is divisible by 2 if the last digit is even; by 3 if digit-sum is divisible by 3; by 4 if the last two digits form a number divisible by 4; by 5 if it ends in 0 or 5; by 9 if digit-sum is divisible by 9; by 11 using alternating digit sum.

steps.title: Apply the rule
hints: Check which digit-sum is a multiple of 9.

steps.title: Remainders
steps.content: When a = bq + r with 0 ≤ r < b, r is the remainder. Remainder questions often combine modular thinking: if n = 5k + 2, then n+3 = 5k + 5 = 5(k+1), remainder 0 when divided by 5.

steps.title: Remainder chain
steps.prompt: A number leaves remainder 3 when divided by 7. What is the remainder when the same number plus 11 is divided by 7?

steps.title: Check divisibility by 11
steps.prompt: Order the steps to test whether 918082 is divisible by 11.
options: Compare the alternating sum to a multiple of 11
Conclude divisibility if the result is 0, ±11, ±22, …

questions.prompt: A number is divisible by 4 if:
options: Its digit sum is divisible by 4
Its last digit is divisible by 4
The number formed by its last two digits is divisible by 4
questions.explanation: Divisibility by 4 depends on the last two digits.

questions.prompt: n leaves remainder 5 when divided by 8. Remainder when n+3 is divided by 8?
Digit sum of 4572 is 18. Divisible by 9?

questions.explanation: 0 is a whole number, not a natural number.

learning_objectives: Classify numbers into natural, whole, integer, rational

common_misconceptions.correction: In most Indian exam keys, natural numbers start at 1; 0 is whole.

company_applications.practice: Divisibility + remainder in one multi-choice item.

srs_cards.question: Rule for divisibility by 3?
srs_cards.answer: Sum of digits is divisible by 3.

srs_cards.question: Rule for divisibility by 11?
srs_cards.answer: Alternating digit sum is a multiple of 11 (including 0).
